items.stem: State any three instruments of the money market.
items.answer: Treasury bill; Commercial paper; Call money; Certificate of deposit; Commercial bill
items.markingKey: Any three of: Treasury bill; Commercial paper; Call money; Certificate of deposit; Commercial bill (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the instruments of the capital market?
items.answer: Certificate of deposit
items.markingKey: (c) "Certificate of deposit" is one of the instruments of the money market, not one of the instruments of the capital market.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The money market deals in long-term funds.
Reason (R): Money market instruments have a maturity of up to one year.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false; R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem: An instrument with a minimum amount of ₹25,000 is issued at a discount by the government and repaid at par. Which money market instrument is described?
items.answer: Treasury bill
items.markingKey: (b) Treasury bill. T-bills are zero-coupon bonds.

items.stem: During a period of tight liquidity, a bank issues a negotiable bearer instrument to mobilise large funds. Which money market instrument is described? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Certificate of deposit. CDs are issued by banks when deposit growth is low.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Certificate of deposit; 2 marks for the justification: CDs are issued by banks when deposit growth is low.

items.stem:
Bank A was short of cash on Friday and borrowed from Bank B until Monday. Meanwhile, Sethi Industries, a large creditworthy bicycles company, issued an unsecured note for 90 days to meet its seasonal needs.
(i) Identify the two money market instruments. (ii) State one feature of each.
items.answer: (i) Call money (inter-bank loan repayable on demand); commercial paper (unsecured promissory note by a large company). (ii) Call money: maturity of 1 to 15 days; commercial paper: negotiable and transferable by endorsement and delivery, 15 days to one year.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Call money (inter-bank loan repayable on demand); commercial paper (unsecured promissory note by a large company). (ii) Call money: maturity of 1 to 15 days; commercial paper: negotiable and transferable by endorsement and delivery, 15 days to one year.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the money market is correct?
items.answer: Commercial paper is an unsecured promissory note.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: Commercial paper is an unsecured promissory note.
options: Treasury bills are issued at a premium.
Certificates of deposit are issued by the stock exchange.
Call money has a maturity of five years.
Commercial paper is an unsecured promissory note.

items.stem:
Tara saves money in shares and bonds through a broker. The money reaches Joshi Retail, which uses it to build a new plant. She can sell the shares any time, the price is set by demand and supply, and brokerage is low.
(i) Identify the market and four functions it performs in the case.
items.answer: (i) Financial market: mobilisation of savings and channelising them into productive uses; providing liquidity; facilitating price discovery; reducing the cost of transactions.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Financial market: mobilisation of savings and channelising them into productive uses; providing liquidity; facilitating price discovery; reducing the cost of transactions.

items.stem: Mishra and Sons draws a bill on its buyer of garments; the accepted bill is discounted with a bank to get cash. Which money market instrument is described?
items.answer: Commercial bill
items.markingKey: (a) Commercial bill. A trade bill discounted with a bank becomes a commercial bill.

items.stem: What is meant by "Primary market"?
items.answer: The new issues market, where new securities are sold for the first time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: The new issues market, where new securities are sold for the first time.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of money market but not of capital market?
items.answer: Expected return: lower

items.stem: Explain the following methods of floatation in the primary market: (i) e-IPOs (ii) Private placement.
items.answer: (i) e-IPOs: Securities are issued through the online system of a stock exchange. (ii) Private placement: Securities are allotted to institutional investors and selected individuals.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) Securities are issued through the online system of a stock exchange. (ii) Securities are allotted to institutional investors and selected individuals.

items.answer: e-IPOs

items.stem: Reddy Traders, a newly listed company, raised funds quickly and cheaply by allotting shares to a few insurance companies. Which method of floatation is used? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Private placement. It avoids the cost of a public issue.

items.stem:
Saxena Industries issued shares to the public for the first time. A year later, Tara bought 100 of those shares from another investor through a stock broker.
(i) Identify the markets involved in the two transactions. (ii) State two differences between them.
items.answer: (i) First issue: primary market; purchase from another investor: secondary market. (ii) Primary deals in new securities, secondary in existing ones; primary prices are fixed by the company, secondary prices by demand and supply; primary directly promotes capital formation.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) First issue: primary market; purchase from another investor: secondary market. (ii) Primary deals in new securities, secondary in existing ones; primary prices are fixed by the company, secondary prices by demand and supply; primary directly promotes capital formation.

items.stem:
Verma Enterprises needs ₹50 crore for 10 years and ₹2 crore for 60 days.
(i) In which market should each amount be raised? (ii) Distinguish between the two markets on four bases.
items.answer: (i) ₹50 crore: capital market; ₹2 crore for 60 days: money market. (ii) Duration (up to one year vs more than one year); instruments (CP, T-bills vs shares, debentures); liquidity (high vs lower); safety and return (safer, lower return vs riskier, higher return).
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) ₹50 crore: capital market; ₹2 crore for 60 days: money market. (ii) Duration (up to one year vs more than one year); instruments (CP, T-bills vs shares, debentures); liquidity (high vs lower); safety and return (safer, lower return vs riskier, higher return).

items.stem: Aditya needed money urgently and sold his shares within minutes through the stock exchange. Which function of a stock exchange is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Providing liquidity and marketability to existing securities. Securities can be converted into cash easily.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Providing liquidity and marketability to existing securities; 2 marks for the justification: Securities can be converted into cash easily.

items.stem: State one difference between primary market and secondary market on the basis of participants.
items.answer: primary market: companies sell to investors; secondary market: investors trade among themselves
items.markingKey: 1 mark: primary market: companies sell to investors; secondary market: investors trade among themselves

items.stem: Bose Traders allotted its shares to mutual funds and banks without going to the public. Which method of floatation is used?
items.answer: Private placement
items.markingKey: (a) Private placement. Securities go to selected institutional investors.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about SEBI is NOT correct?
items.answer: SEBI is a private association of stock brokers.
items.markingKey: (a) Incorrect statement: SEBI is a private association of stock brokers.
options: SEBI is a private association of stock brokers.
Registering mutual funds is a regulatory function of SEBI.
Training of intermediaries is a developmental function of SEBI.
Controlling insider trading is a protective function of SEBI.

items.stem: What is meant by "Screen-based trading"?
items.answer: Electronic trading in which buyers and sellers interact through computers instead of on a trading floor.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Electronic trading in which buyers and sellers interact through computers instead of on a trading floor.
